To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the red blood cell calcium uptake is enhanced by the incubation of red blood cells with the oxidizing agent diamide, 2) this effect is due to the membrane alteration caused by the oxidation of some thiol groups, and 3) the red blood cells calcium uptake is restored to control values after the reduction of the oxidized groups with dithioerythrol.
diamide treatment of red blood cells causes the loss of calcium‐transporting ability and that the loss is restored to control values by incubation with dithioerythrol.
the diamide effect on the calcium uptake by rat blood cells is linearly dependent on diamide concentration and osmolarity of incubation medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a new class of membrane perturbing agents, the diazenedicarbo‐xamides, on the calcium transport in rat red blood cells.
a new aspect of the red blood cell membrane, which is the presence of a thiol‐dependent calcium transport system.
the study of the effect of a chemical agent on the red blood cells calcium uptake in the presence of hypertonicity.

diamide and DTE are useful tools to investigate membrane structure and function.
, under the conditions of our experiments, diamide and hypertonticity can induce a membrane damage which is reversible by dithioerythrol.
the diamide effect on the red blood cells hypertonic calcium uptake is the consequence of the membrane alteration caused by a thiol‐dependent mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diamide and hypertonticity act in synergy to oxidize some thios involved in the cation barrier.
the red blood cell calcium transport can be modulated by the membrane thiol groups.
the red blood cell cation permeability is increased by diamide and that the effect is enhanced by hypertonic conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the red blood cells calcium uptake is a sensitive indicator of the red blood cells membrane integrity.
diamide, in combination with hypertonicity, is able to oxidize thiol groups in red blood cell membranes and that these thiol groups are important for maintaining the calcium barrier.
diamide can be used in the study of the calcium transport mechanism.
